evidence: Cic. Off. 1.153: prūdentia … est rērum expetendārum fugiendārumque scientia
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “sagacity, good sense, intelligence, prudence, practical judgment”.
Sī sapis, if you have any sense.
Plain common sense in Phaedrus; in Cicero and Horace rather tact, a feeling for others (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Sen. Ep. 27.8: bona mēns nec commodātur nec emitur

terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to recover one’s senses, come to one’s self again … become reasonable”.

phrases.latin: Manē, manē, jam ut volēs mēd esse ita erō. — Nunc tū sapis.
phrases.english: Wait, wait, I’ll be just as you want me. — Now you’re talking sense.

phrases.latin: bona mēns nec commodātur nec emitur
phrases.english: Good sense can be neither borrowed nor bought.

phrases.latin: Hoc illīs dictum est, quibus honōrem et glōriam Fortūna tribuit, sēnsum commūnem abstulit.
phrases.english: This is said for those to whom Fortune has given honour and glory, and taken away common sense.
